title: Baker Boy Takes Album, Song and Film Clip of the Year at 2026 NIMAs
summary: The Yolŋu rapper first broke through in 2017 after winning triple j's Unearthed National Indigenous Music Awards competition.
body: Baker Boy was the dominant winner at the 2026 National Indigenous Music Awards, taking home three of the night’s top prizes at a ceremony held Saturday (Aug. 8) at the Darwin Amphitheater. The Yolŋu rapper won Album of the Year for DJANDJAY , while his single “THICK SKIN” — featuring Thelma Plum, Emma Donovan, Kee’ahn and Jada Weazel — claimed both Song of the Year and Film Clip of the Year. Baker Boy performed the track live at the ceremony, bringing out Donovan as a surprise guest. Cousin duo Birdz and Fred Leone won Artist of the Year, their first NIMA, on the strength of their debut EP GIRA . Drifting Clouds took Best New Talent, Northern Peninsula Area won Community Clip of the Year for “All The Way From The NPA,” and Bulman School & Community earned the Indigenous Language Award for “LOK LOK MAH BURARR” (Lizard & Goanna). As previously announced, blues musician Marlene Cummins and Elcho Island’s Saltwater Band were inducted into the NIMAs Hall of Fame, with the night closing on a tribute to the band. “Last night’s celebration brought together some of the most incredible music and musicians this country…

title: aespa Kicks Off SYNK : COMPLæXITY Tour in Seoul: 6 Best Moments
summary: aespa opened its fourth world tour at with 27 songs, an expanded universe and a show that brought the group's many sides into full view.
body: Seoul was already deep in the heat of August when thousands of MYs made their way to Gocheok Sky Dome for the opening weekend of aespa ‘s fourth world tour. Inside, the temperature only seemed to rise. Across Aug. 7 and 8, Karina, Winter, Giselle and Ningning welcomed a combined 35,000 fans to aespa’s first concerts at the dome, opening SYNK : COMPLæXITY with 27 songs across roughly two-and-a-half hours. Built around “CRACK,” a rupture that brings aespa into conflict with altered versions of ae-aespa, the show unfolds through five chapters: singularity, intrusion, confinement, awakening and resolution. New songs from LEMONADE , which debuted at No. 9 on the Billboard 200 in June as the group’s third top 10 entry on the chart, sit alongside defining hits, solo and unit stages, cinematic VCRs and large-scale choreography. summary: Fenix Flexin also joined the Aug. 7 concert, which marked the end of the This Is Our Dream Tour.
body: Puebla York was in the building on Friday night (Aug. 7), braving a heavy thunderstorm to see Fuerza Regida close its first-ever U.S. stadium tour at New York’s Citi Field with a guest lineup that brought corridos bélicos and hip-hop into the same orbit — connecting the West Coast and East Coast with unusual ease. summary: The iconic R&B acts didn’t let the rain stop their parade, as they delivered more than 50 songs and brought out some of New York’s favorite legends.
body: On Friday night (Aug. 7), a menacing cluster of clouds and thunderstorms sought to play spoiler ahead of Chris Brown and Usher’s Raymond & Brown Tour performance at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey. The venue that hosted the 2026 World Cup less than a month ago on a balmy Sunday afternoon was hit by torrential rain that could have KO’d the entire show. Fortunately, the rain subsided, allowing a throng of R&B lovers to trek from the five boroughs and various counties in New Jersey to see a once-in-a-lifetime tour. A smattering of howls and cheers filled the stadium as fans eagerly waited for their arrival. Since June, Brown and Raymond have already delivered viral gold with their nostalgic efforts, thrilling performances and racy escapades. The blockbuster trek comes on the heels of Brown’s career-defining Breezy Bowl Stadium Tour , which featured Jhené Aiko, Summer Walker and Bryson Tiller, while this run is Usher’s first since his Past Present Future Tour in 2024. summary: Additionally, Marc Anthony & Yandel will be honored as Agents of Change at Premios Juventud.
body: From career milestones to new releases to major announcements and those little important moments, Billboard editors highlight uplifting moments in Latin music. Here’s what happened in the Latin music world this week. Mon Laferte to Receive Social Justice Award This week, it was announced that Mon Laferte will receive the Social Justice Award at the 39th annual Hispanic Heritage Awards, taking place Sept. 10 at Orchestra Hall in Minneapolis. The Chilean singer will be honored for using her art, music and platforms to promote conversations about human rights, gender equality and social justice in Latin America and around the world. “I feel incredibly honored. I never imagined that a moment would come in my life or career when my work to carry out the projects that truly matter to me would be recognized,” Laferte said in a statement. “I believe one of the greatest strengths of the Latino community is our ability to build connections, welcome and care for one another, wherever we may be. title: Vera Blue covers Radiohead’s ‘Creep’ for triple j’s Like A Version
summary: Blue also performed "Maze," a track from her forthcoming album Modern Rituals.
body: Vera Blue has taken on one of alternative rock’s most enduring songs, covering Radiohead ‘s “Creep” for triple j’s Like A Version . The Australian singer-songwriter stripped the 1992 track back to three elements — electric guitar, piano and vocals — building from the lower end of her range into a soaring falsetto by the chorus. Late in the performance she deployed The Pipe, a mouth-controlled dynamic effects processor and synthesizer made by SOMA Laboratory, adding an eerie texture to the arrangement. Blue said she was drawn to the song’s emotional core, describing “Creep” as an “epic rock song” whose lyrics are also “heartbreaking,” and aiming for a “very haunting version” that still nods to Thom Yorke’s original. Blue also performed “Maze,” a track from her forthcoming album Modern Rituals , during her studio session. The album is due Friday, Aug. 21 via Island Records/Universal Music Australia, and Blue will support it with a national tour opening the same night at Brisbane’s Princess Theatre and running through Perth’s The Rechabite on Aug. 28. title: Brandi Carlile Postpones U.K. and European Tour Citing ‘Personal Circumstances’
summary: The run, originally set to begin in October, has been pushed to March 2027.
body: Brandi Carlile has postponed the UK and European leg of her tour, citing “personal circumstances,” the singer-songwriter announced on social media Friday (Aug. 7). The run, originally set to begin in October, has been pushed to March 2027. Carlile did not specify the reason beyond describing it as a personal matter. View this post on Instagram “I have been so profoundly anxious about this decision, and I’m aware that this change may be disappointing and inconvenient for many of you, especially those of you who were planning on traveling internationally,” she wrote, adding that she hoped the rescheduling would give fans time to adjust their plans. “I want nothing more than to see my friends across the pond and I have done everything in my power to avoid rescheduling this tour.” The postponement affects several dates. Carlile’s Lisbon show has been canceled outright, while two new dates in Wolverhampton, England, and Copenhagen have been added.
